name: m6_my_voice_oui_3

spec.name: m6_my_voice_oui_3
spec.brief: The user's own voice as a filter. Morph 0 is their 'oo', Morph 1 their 'ee', so the morph says 'oui'. Q opens to their 'aa' under Morph 0 and closes to their 'nn' hum under Morph 1. Targets are cepstrally smoothed spectra of the recordings with +6 dB per octave to take the voice source's slope out. The two lowest lanes trade poles across Morph, as Talking Hedz does. Second pass: the ee, aa and oo recordings are whispered, so no slope correction is applied to them (+6 dB per octave only on the voiced hums); every target is held flat below 0.6 x its first peak, because the recording's roll-off down there is microphone and radiation, not the mouth, and a vocal tract is flat towards DC. Version 2, closing the gap to the factory preset heard beside it: the band runs to 10 kHz so the spare poles have the whisper's real top end to draw instead of parking at the band edge, and the Q 1 corners are narrowed to 40 Hz so Q sharpens as well as changing the vowel. Version 3: the one authored zero pair, the zero on the unit circle, is tuned to the voice. In each corner it sits at the deepest point of that recording's own spectrum between 4 and 12 kHz, so it moves with Morph and Q as the factory's does, at frequencies taken from the user and not from any factory preset. The other ten zeros are solved around it.
